October 2009 # A pause or a turning point - Rising exchange stocks, falling premiums and disappointing post-summer demand are all signs that indicate a possible turning point in the physical copper market. - But Exchange markets are not convinced, and prices have recovered in the past few days, supported by the weaker dollar and positive macro economic news out of China. Even though inventories on the LME are on the rise, they are still at historically low levels. - Production shows signs of improvement although the possibility of looming strikes could derail this trend and lend some support to the price. |The supply/demand

Foreca|st produ|ction allo|ws for p|otential|| © 2009 CRU International Limited **confidential** October 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** # Tug of war The copper market continues to surprise on the upside, and still appears to contradict the fundamentals. Bearish views as regards to the price have clearly been wrong over most of this year, amongst which CRU‟s view has been counted. Prices have remained decidedly volatile and there are no reasons to expect this to change as the market continues to react to favourable future interpretations of current macro economic news and remains far ahead of today‟s underlying demand. Towards the end of last week, however, the market took on a bearish tone. The diminishing pace of Chinese refined i

mports, rising LME inventories and no sign of the seasonal September upturn in demand derailed copper‟s upward path. Three month prices slipped toward $5,850/t by late September after peaking at a high of $6,540/t at the Are prices finally

end of August, suggesting that the market finally appears to be reacting to the slow and steady increase in inventories. Total exchange inventories increased by a further 56,000t in September. LME stocks accounted for the majority of the increase (46,000t), the bulk of which has been built up at Asian warehouses. Stocks are now off the recent lows. Prices continue to track movements in equities, which in turn are being influenced by the macro economic calendar. With a significant amount of doubt about the short term outlook, the price will be a fickle beast. This week, despite further deliveries into the LME, the price has recouped some of its recent losses. There are a few factors that may account for this latest move above $6,100/t; Shanghai stocks fell for two consecutive weeks despite the approach of the extended National Holiday in China and weaker local premiums; the dollar weakened further against the euro; some short covering; and news that the Chinese PMI index rose in September to 54.3, its highest level in over a year and the seventh consecutive monthly rise, signalling sustained strength in activity. These factors, alongside news that workers at BHPB‟s Spence copper mine have opted for strike action, have boosted prices, which were trading close to $6,150/t at the time of writing. ## **Physical the new financial** As we highlighted last month, commodity assets under management have increased. The latest issuer to enter the commodity space is ScotiaMocatta with its Physical Copper Fund that is looking to tap into institution investor interest. Its purpose is to buy and sell copper. According to the prospectus, "The trust ... has been created to provide holders of units with direct exposure to the price performance of physical copper." At the other extreme, George Soros has acquired as 20% share of a copper mine. These developments only up the debate that copper is increasingly viewed as a financial asset. ## **Consumer restocking hindered by high prices and lack of clarity** Our research in recent weeks in Europe and Asia has highlighted two trends. Firstly, demand did not pick up in the third quarter, particularly in Europe where offtake usually improves following the summerholiday lull. Secondly, high copper prices are deterring consumer r

estocking. Not only are consumers unwilling to carry any inventory (most destocked any available metal in Q4 2008 and the first half of this © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 October 2009 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com year), but they are continuing to live on a hand-to-mouth basis despite demand having hit bottom. Looking ahead this trend is unlikely to change given the fragile economic outlook. European copper demand in particular has been dealt a heavy blow with the announcement last week which will see Nexans‟ largest rod mill (250,000tpy) at Chauny close by the year end and shed around 400 jobs. Nexans will cease producing extra wire for sale and only produce what it requires internally. The closure of Chauny will leave only the Lens 150,000tpy capacity in production and result in a sharp slump in refined copper demand in France in 2010. Workers have unofficially downed tools at Chauny in protest against the announcement and production has stopped. Producers selling into France will now have to find another market for their cathode. So who will benefit from the withdrawal of this wirerod capacity? We anticipate that Aurubis‟ facilities in Hamburg and Belgium will most certainly pick up market share. The balance of trade will also shift, as Nexans had been exporting copper rod to both Spain and Italy. Traders will also have to find another route as they will no longer be able to toll material through Chauny. The power cable market is generally healthy on the back of government spending plans, although the market for wire and cable into the European construction, automotive and electronics (consumer goods) sectors remain lacklustre due to the global economic downturn. ## **Some signs of recovery** The industrialising economies have now taken up the baton of demand from the traditional consuming regions of Europe and the USA. In China the rod sector is booming. In August alone, 400,000t/y of new capacity came on stream with significant additional capacity due on stream over the balance of the year |and in 2010. The high voltage cable sector is still busy. Luvata‟s recent announcement that idled capacity in the USA and Europe will restart suggests that the brass mill sector is coming back, albeit belatedly and driven mainly by the air conditioner sector. With the worst seemingly over for copper semis producers, we would expect to see consecutive monthly improvements in refined demand in Q4. Spot premiums in Europe have been quoted in the $60-70/t range but these are nominal given the dearth of spot business over the past month. The spot premium in China for imported copper cathodes has dropped recently to $30-70/t (previously $30-90/t) reflecting the quiet trading activity ahead of the © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 October 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** National Holiday. Premiums in the USA are in a broader range of 3.5-5.0¢/lb, compared to last month, amid easier scrap availability. Recent Chilean tenders also confirm the soft tone. Pucobre sold 300t of unregistered cathode for $60/t and 500t of Pucobre-rejects was sold at a discount of $15/t. Both parcels were for October shipment, November QP. Codelco sold 4,000t standard grade cathode (2,000t/m October and November shipment) in mid-September at a $44/t discount, QP M+1. ## **Mating season approaches** As we approach the period of traditional courtship between the producers and consumers, there is still no clarity as to the prospects for demand. These murky waters suggest that producers will face another difficult round of negotiations when they meet their customers following LME week. Reports suggest that Codelco‟s benchmark European premium will remain at $80/t. It is certainly not a foregone conclusion that these terms will be accepted by consumers, but this does reflect the prevailing terms currently available for spot material. No premium has been suggested for Asia or the USA. Given that recovery in demand is far advanced in Asia and the Middle East, producers wil

l try and push through higher premiums for those regions in 2010, especially as they now account for the dominant 58% share of the world market. ## **Codelco continues to perform** The only disruption to production over the past month was the rock fall at Newmont‟s Batu Hijau mine. Estimates suggest that output could be down by as much as 30%. However, we think it unlikely given that there should be sufficient stockpiles to maintain mill throughput at the current annual level of 32Mt, i.e. 200,000t copper-in-concentrate. Meanwhile, the latest output data for Codelco suggest improved performance at most of its operations and not just a reflection of Gaby‟s ongoing ramp up. We await Q3 results to confirm the recovery seen in H1. Q4 should see additional output with the resurgence of mining in the Zambian Copperbelt (Nkana, Mufulira, Baluba mines) and the ramp up at Tenke, Boddington, Franke, Prominent Hill, Las Cruces and Lumwana mines. However, the breakdown of labour negotiations at BHPB‟s Spence and the decision by workers to opt for strike action could lead to some disruption to supply in the coming weeks. Workers at Chuquicamata, Escondida and Los Bronces will be closely watching the outcome at Spence, in preparation for their discussions when their Q4 – Down this year too? contracts are due for renewal at the end of the Monthly copper prices 2004-2009 year. The outcome at Spence will be considered as the benchmark for the region. **2008** 2008

## **Conflicting arguments** After reacting so dramatically to last autumn‟s meltdown, copper appears to be settling down now, although given the pattern over the past few years we expect Q4 to be a weaker period for prices. Higher stocks and weak demand are engaged in a tug of war with an erratic dollar, positive macro sentiment and China. Without the support of China for the next eight days it will be macro economic data and potential production developments that will steer prices in the short term. A lot of people talk about recovery now. What we see is a lot of smoke that we need to interpret. We do not have definitive signals. The only definitive signal is that the fall is over." -Domenico Cova, KME Group, Italy (Reuters interview, 18th September) ## **Developed world still accounts for more than 40% of global demand** CRU estimates that the „developed‟ countries of the world (North America, Western Europe, North East Asia and Australasia) will account for about 42% of global refined copper demand in 2009, down from 47% in 2008. After a precipitous decline in late 2008/early 2009 refined demand in the developed world has stabilised in recent months as fabricators have finished destocking and have begun to increase semis output in response to growth in end-use demand. Most fabricators in these countries appear to believe that demand has reached its floor, but a strong recovery is not anticipated. Volumes are expected to remain steady for the balance of this year, with a modest recovery in demand occurring in 2010. However, there remains Refined copper demand in developed

For instance, demand from the automotive sector has been temporarily boosted due to scrappage schemes, but may fall again as these come to an end. In addition, a number of effects of the downt

urn have yet to play out, unemployment, for instance, is still rising in many countries, which will restrain the growth in consumer spending on copper-containing goods. ## **Semis output improves in North East Asia** South Korea has been the star performer among developed countries this year, with semis production rising by 0.8% in the first seven months. In July, semis production was up 12.3% y-o-y to 116,703t, a remarkable turn around from a 31.8% y-o-y decline in January. The increase in production has mostly been driven by increased output of wirerod, which has benefitted from strong growth in exports to China. Demand in Taiwan has also recovered since the start of the year, with production at 64,344t in July, having climbed from a low of 28,683t in January. Japanese rolled copper product output was up 2.2% m-o-m in August to 63,344t. Demand has improved from the automotive and semiconductor sectors. However, demand is still down 21% y-o-y and copper consumption is NE Asian semis production recovers

Japan‟s leading copper smelter, Pan Pacific Copper, reports that it is seeing sequential month-on-month improvements in domestic demand. Along with strong export demand, this has meant that it has been able to reduce output less than feared, with a 4-5% y-o-y cut in April-September. ## **US semis production has also steadied** US semis production has also stabilised. The latest data from the American Bureau of Metal Statistics reports that US output of copper wirerod was 99,367t in June, an increase of 1.5% m-o-m. US production is benefitting from improved domestic consumption, as well as reduced imports of Russian wirerod. According to the Copper and Brass Servicecenter Association, copper shipments were up 9.4% m-o-m and copper alloy shipments up 15% m-o-m in July. Fabricators reported, however, that the market was still „bouncing on the bottom‟. ## **European fabricators expect modest recovery in 2010** Leading European semis fabricators and smelters anticipate a subdued recovery in end-use demand in 2010. Italian statistical body Assomet expects that production of semis will recover 4.8% y-o-y in 2010 to 968,300t, still far short of 2008 production after an estimated 22.3% y-o-y fall in output in 2009. s|e mont|hs, seas|onally| © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 9 of 12 October 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** # Industry News ## **Production** - On 23rd September, workers at **BHP Billiton** ‟s **Spence** mine rejected the company‟s proposal for the renegotiation of the collective labour contract. This is the first renewal since the mine started-up in 2006. BHP Billiton proposed to adjust the previous wages in accordance with inflation, but workers asked for a 5.5% increase. Workers vote on whether to accept the company proposal or go on strike and opted to strike. However, there is a five day mediation period before they can walk out, so the strike is not yet definite. The existing contract expired on 26th September 2009. The result of this labour contract negotiation will set a precedent for other large mines in the region - **Escondida** and **Chuquicamata** - whose workers are also threatening industrial action when their contracts come up for renewal later this year. In 2009, Spence is expected to produce 185,000t of copper cathode. - On 18th and 19th September there was a “geotechnical failure” in the west wall of the open-pit of the **Batu Hijau** mine. Following the landslides, **Newmont Mining** announced that operations at the mine will be suspended, but production will not be affected as there is stock piled material which can be processed. Batu Hijau is due to produce 207,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2009. - It was reported on 1st September, that a federal bankruptcy judge endorsed the reorganisation plan offered by **Grupo Mexico** (Mexico), and thus recommended that Grupo Mexico be allowed to take control of **Asarco** (USA). A final decision is expected in October. The latest bid for Asarco made by Grupo Mexico was US$2.480B, which would be sufficient to repay all of Asasrco‟s creditors. **Sterlite Industries’** (India) latest bid is US$2.565B, but a further increase was rejected by the judge on the grounds that it was submitted too late, according to press reports. - In mid-September, it was reported that **Mopani Copper Mines (MCM)** would reverse the plan to put the **Mufulira** and **Nkana** mines on a care and maintenance basis given that the copper price had recovered and passed US$5,500/t. In 2009, the Mufulira and Nkana are expected to produce 35,000t and 62,000t, respectively, of copper-in-concentrate; and 15,000t and 10,000t of copper cathode. - On 23rd September, **Katanga Mining** (Canada) announced it has completed the acquisition of **Kamoto Operating Limited (KOL),** which operates the assets of **Kamoto Copper Company** in the DR Congo. The total value of the transaction is estimated at US$8.22M according to press reports. Previously, Katanga Mining said they would accelerate the ramp-up of the **Kamoto Concentrator** and the **Luilu Refinery**

to Q2 2011 from Q1 2013 as the company holds enough cash.  In 2009 Katanga Mining is expected to produce 46,000t of copper cathode. 

- On 18<sup>th</sup> September, a fire damaged the 720MW Kariba North Bank power station disrupting 540MW of capacity.  However, copper and cobalt mines in the Zambian Copperbelt where not disrupted. 

- On 18<sup>th</sup> September, **Eurasian Natural Resources Corp (ENRC)** and **Central African Mining of Exploration (CAMEC)** announced they have agreed to recommend a cash offer for a subsidiary of ENRC to fully acquire CAMEC Plc.  The offer values the entire issued and yet to be issued share capital of CAMEC for a total of £584M (~US$955M). 

## **Exploration and Development** 



- In mid-September, **Codelco** approved a US$52M investment to start the feasibility study for the **El Teniente – New Level** project (Chile).  The expansion project aims to start in 2017 and will extend

- the life of the mine to 50 years.  In addition, this year the company is investing US$256M at this operation and has approved an increase in the budget to US$367M for 2010.  These investments aim to expand operations and improve their processing facilities.  Without this, El Teniente would cease operations by 2025.  In 2009, El Teniente is expected to produce 342,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 





- On 24<sup>th</sup> September, **China Metallurgical Group Corporation (CMGC)** announced that, jointly with **Jiangxi Copper Corporation (JCC)** , they will develop the **Afghan Aynak Copper Mine** (Afghanistan).  The removal of landmines planted during the Russian occupation of Afghanistan started in June and is due to be completed in December 2010.  Construction will then commence in 2011 and Phase 1 will produce 180,000t of copper-in-concentrates.  After a Phase 2 expansion, the project will produce over 300,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates. 

- It was reported that the **Wunugetu Copper & Molybdenum Mine** project (Inner Mongolia Region – China) has started trial production. **Inner Mongolia Mining Company** (owned by **China National Group Gold Corporation** ) invested RMB2.8B (~ US$415M).  The average ore grades are 0.46%Cu and 0.055%Mo. At full capacity, the project is expected to process 30,000t/d of ore and produce over 140,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 











- On 31<sup>st</sup> August **, Konkola Copper Mines (KCM)** , majority owned by **Vedanta Resources** , confirmed that it would shut down its **Nchanga** smelter (Zambia) for three weeks from on 1<sup>st</sup> September.  The shutdown is for scheduled maintenance with a ramp-up to normal production expected after three weeks.  This closure follows a technical failure that occurred on 27<sup>th</sup> June, and which caused operations to be suspended for about two weeks.  The Nchanga smelter, which began operation

s late last year, has the capacity to produce 250,000t/y of copper anode.  CRU expects it will produce no more than 100,000t of copper anode this year. 

- In late September, it was reported that the **Chambishi** smelter (Chinese-owned) will process 55% of the annual copper concentrates production of the **Lumwana mine (Equinox Minerals)** .  Earlier this year, Lumwana‟s copper concentrates were rejected by **Mopani Copper Mines** , cited high uranium traces as the reason for its rejection.  In 2009, Chambishi is expected to produce 45,000t of copper blister. 

- In mid-September, it was reported that **Pan Pacific Copper** plans to continue output cuts because of the difficulties in the procurement of copper concentrates.  Earlier this year, the company announced production cutbacks due to the weak demand.  Its production was reduced by 10% in January-March and by 4-5% in April-September. 

- It was reported that on 27<sup>th</sup> August, **China Second Metallurgical Construction Co (CSMCC)** started operations at a 100,000t/d-capacity smelter in Ximengxiwuqui (Inner Mongolia-China). 

- In late August, **Xstrata** announced that it will temporarily close its **Kidd Creek** smelter due to a shortage of concentrates.  Workers at the **Sudbury** and **Voisey’s Bay** mines, owned by **Vale Inco** , have been on strike since July and August, respectively.  This has been restricting copper concentrates supply to Kidd Creek.  The shutdown is expected to last between seven and ten weeks. This closure follows an 8-week summer holiday shutdown, attributed to a weak sulphuric acid demand.  Kidd Creek produced 87,000t of blister copper in 2008, though its capacity is nearer 165,000t/y.

- The Peruvian National Congress granted to **Doe Run Peru** (a unit of the US-based **Renco Group** ) a 30-month extension to fulfil its environmental commitments at **La Oroya** smelter. Previously, the company had to complete its commitments by October 2009 or it would loose its operating license. In 2009, La Oroya is expected to produce 38,000t of copper blister. 

## **Consumption** 









- **Nexans** , the **French** cable maker, announced that it will reduce its workforce in France by some 400 jobs and close its copper wirerod mill in **Chauny** , northern France.  The decision of the company will affect its plants in **Clichy** , **Fumay** , **Jeumont** , **Lyon** and **Mehun** .  The group aims to cut costs by merging the activities of **Nexans France** and **Nexans Copper France** , creating 50 new jobs. 

- **Prysmian** (Italy) and **Draka** (Dutch), cable makers, both issued press releases announcing the end of talks regarding a potential merger between them.  The potential combination was announced in June 2009 and would have taken place through a share cross-border statutory merger with Prysmian as surviving entity.  Both parties co

mmented that the deal was terminated after failure to reach an agreement on terms and conditions.  Prysmian said that it has €1 billion in liquidity, and is looking for acquisitions in regions of high growth, such as Russia, India and China. 

- Wire and cable shipments in **Japan** contracted by 17.7% y-o-y to 50,100t in August.  The figures were released by the **Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers’ Association** .  Even though there are signs that the market is improving m-o-m, the figure indicates that the widely expected economic recovery is not yet solidly based. 

- **KME** , the **Italian** copper and alloy semis fabricator, is anticipating that sales in 2009 will plunge by 30% compared with the previous year.  The company expects that demand for its products will recover in 2010 by 10-15% y-o-y.  KME reported that demand from the automotive industry has improved, supported by government aid.
